questions.q: Which of the following statements is true?
questions.answer: Each amino acid in a protein is coded for by three bases in the DNA.
distractors: Each DNA base codes for three amino acids.
It takes three genes to code for one protein.
Each triplet has many different meanings.
Each gene codes for three proteins.

questions.q: In transcription, how many of the DNA strands are used as the template?
questions.answer: Only one of the DNA strands
distractors: Both DNA strands at the same time
Both DNA strands, taking turns
Neither; RNA is copied from another RNA
Neither; the template is a protein

questions.q: In transcription, what acts as the initial binding site for RNA polymerase?
questions.answer: The promoter region
distractors: The enhancer region
The ribosome
The start codon
The anticodon
The replication fork

questions.q: The number of nucleotide bases "read" together on the mRNA to designate each amino acid is _____; this unit is called a(n) _____.
questions.answer: three ... codon
distractors: three ... triose
two ... dipeptide
one ... amino acid
two ... anticodon

questions.q: During translation in a eukaryotic cell _____.
questions.answer: polypeptides are synthesized at ribosomes, according to instructions carried by mRNA
distractors: ribosomes move into the nucleus
tRNA carries amino acid molecules to the nucleus, where they are added to a growing polypeptide chain
ribosomes move out of the nucleus
mRNA is synthesized by the bonding of free nucleotides to the bases on the template strand of DNA

questions.q: The function of tRNA during protein synthesis is to _____.
questions.answer: deliver amino acids to their proper site during protein synthesis
distractors: transcribe mRNA
process mRNA
attach mRNA to the small subunit of the ribosome
guide ribosome subunits out of the nucleus through nuclear pores

questions.q: In a eukaryotic cell, transcription takes place _____.
questions.answer: in the nucleus
distractors: on free ribosomes
on the cell membrane
in the rough endoplasmic reticulum
in the cytoplasm

questions.q: What is a key difference in gene expression between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells?
questions.answer: In prokaryotic cells, the mRNA transcript is immediately available as mRNA without processing.
distractors: In eukaryotic cells, transcribed RNA sequences function as termination signals.
RNA polymerases are involved only in initiation in eukaryotes.
Prokaryotes do not contain ribosomes.
In prokaryotes, proteins are assembled directly from DNA.

questions.q: In a eukaryote, activating transcription factors may stimulate gene expression by binding to a DNA site called a(n) _____.
questions.answer: enhancer
distractors: histone
promoter
operon
silencer

questions.q: Which of the following summaries of protein synthesis is correct?
questions.answer: Messenger RNA is made on a DNA template, and then amino-acid-bearing transfer RNAs bind to it through codon-anticodon pairing.
distractors: DNA strands separate in the nucleus to form mRNA. mRNA leaves the nucleus and is transcribed into tRNA on ribosomes.
Transfer RNAs line up on a ribosome, and amino acids bind to them with hydrogen bonds.
DNA exchanges its thymine units with uracil in polymerase. This activates polymerase, and it starts joining amino acids together.
DNA transposons leave the nucleus, are transported to a ribosome, and catalyze the polymerization of amino acids in a protein.

questions.q: What is the proper order of these events in the expression of a eukaryotic gene? (1) translation, (2) RNA processing, (3) transcription, (4) modification of protein
The DNA sequence in a gene is transcribed into an RNA sequence. This stage is called _____.
questions.answer: transcription
distractors: translation
replication
RNA processing
splicing
gene silencing

questions.q: Transcription begins when RNA polymerase binds to a special nucleotide sequence called a(n) _____.
questions.answer: promoter
distractors: enhancer
operator
start codon
anticodon
intron

questions.q: What is the central dogma?
questions.answer: The one-way flow of genetic information in a cell: DNA to RNA to protein
distractors: The one-way flow of genetic information in a cell: protein to RNA to DNA
The one-way flow of genetic information in a cell: RNA to DNA to protein
The rule that each gene codes for exactly one amino acid
The rule that A pairs with T and C pairs with G in DNA
The idea that proteins copy themselves without DNA

questions.q: What is translation?
questions.answer: Ribosomes decoding mRNA to build a chain of amino acids (a polypeptide)
distractors: RNA polymerase copying a DNA sequence into mRNA
DNA polymerase copying DNA to make two DNA molecules
Removing introns and joining exons in a pre-mRNA
Breaking down mRNA so a gene is silenced
Folding a finished protein inside the nucleus

questions.q: The use of information in DNA to direct the production of particular polypeptides is called _____.
questions.answer: gene expression
distractors: DNA replication
alternative splicing
RNA interference
mutation
gene regulation

questions.q: The RNA copy of a gene that the cell uses to produce a polypeptide is called _____.
questions.answer: messenger RNA (mRNA)
distractors: transfer RNA (tRNA)
ribosomal RNA (rRNA)
small interfering RNA (siRNA)
complementary DNA
an anticodon

questions.q: The enzyme that transcribes DNA into RNA is a large and very sophisticated protein called _____.
questions.answer: RNA polymerase
distractors: DNA polymerase
helicase
ligase
reverse transcriptase
ribosomal protein

questions.q: Which RNA nucleotide pairs with adenine (A)?
questions.answer: U (uracil)
distractors: T (thymine)
G (guanine)
C (cytosine)
A (adenine)

questions.q: The rules that govern how mRNA codons are translated into amino acids are called the _____.
questions.answer: genetic code
distractors: central dogma
base-pairing rules
reading frame
operon
proteome

questions.q: What is a codon?
questions.answer: A sequence of three nucleotides that codes for one amino acid or a start/stop signal
distractors: A sequence of three nucleotides on tRNA that pairs with mRNA
A sequence of two nucleotides that codes for one amino acid
A single nucleotide that codes for one amino acid
A DNA site where RNA polymerase binds to start transcription
A section of RNA that is removed before translation

questions.q: What is a ribosome?
questions.answer: The polypeptide-making factory of the cell
distractors: The energy-producing powerhouse of the cell
The control center that stores the cell's DNA
The packaging and shipping center of the cell
The enzyme that copies DNA into RNA
The membrane that controls what enters the cell

questions.q: What is tRNA?
questions.answer: A small RNA molecule that brings amino acids to the ribosome, matching them to mRNA codons
distractors: The RNA copy of a gene that carries instructions out of the nucleus
The RNA that makes up the structure of the ribosome
A small RNA molecule that silences genes by breaking down mRNA
An enzyme that joins nucleotides to make RNA
A noncoding sequence that is removed from pre-mRNA

questions.q: What is an anticodon?
questions.answer: A sequence of three nucleotides on tRNA that pairs with a complementary mRNA codon
distractors: A sequence of three nucleotides on mRNA that codes for an amino acid
A codon that signals the end of translation
A sequence of three amino acids at the start of a protein
A DNA sequence where RNA polymerase binds
A noncoding sequence removed from pre-mRNA

questions.q: What does an anticodon do?
questions.answer: Pairs with a matching mRNA codon by complementary base pairing, like a key in a lock
distractors: Signals RNA polymerase where to start transcription
Joins neighboring amino acids with peptide bonds
Cuts introns out of the pre-mRNA
Carries the gene's instructions out of the nucleus
Tells the ribosome to stop translating

questions.q: What is the product of DNA replication?
questions.answer: Two DNA duplexes
distractors: mRNA
Polypeptides
tRNA
One DNA duplex and one RNA strand
Ribosomes

questions.q: What is the product of transcription?
questions.answer: mRNA
distractors: Two DNA duplexes
Polypeptides
Amino acids
Ribosomes
Anticodons

questions.q: What is the product of translation?
questions.answer: Polypeptides
distractors: mRNA
Two DNA duplexes
tRNA
Nucleotides
Introns

questions.q: What is an exon?
questions.answer: A section of a gene that remains in the mature mRNA after non-coding pieces are removed
distractors: A non-coding section of a gene that is removed from the pre-mRNA
A DNA site where RNA polymerase first binds
A cluster of genes transcribed as a single unit
A sequence of three nucleotides on tRNA
A DNA site, far from a gene, where activators bind

questions.q: What is an intron?
questions.answer: An extraneous, non-coding nucleotide sequence that is removed from the pre-mRNA
distractors: A coding sequence that remains in the mature mRNA
A DNA site where RNA polymerase first binds
A sequence of three nucleotides that codes for an amino acid
A protein that turns off a gene
A cluster of genes transcribed as a single unit

questions.q: What is alternative splicing?
questions.answer: Joining exons from one pre-mRNA in different combinations so one gene can code for several proteins
distractors: Copying both DNA strands so one gene makes two mRNAs
Silencing a gene by breaking down its mRNA before translation
Transcribing a cluster of genes together as one unit
Reading the same mRNA in a different direction to make a new protein
Swapping genes between chromosomes during meiosis

questions.q: What is an operon?
questions.answer: A segment of DNA containing a cluster of genes that are transcribed as a unit
distractors: A single gene that codes for several different proteins
A section of a gene that is removed before translation
A DNA site, far from a gene, where activators bind
A small RNA that turns off a gene
The site on a ribosome where tRNA binds

questions.q: What is an enhancer?
questions.answer: A DNA site, which can be far from the gene, where eukaryotic activators bind
distractors: The DNA site right next to a gene where RNA polymerase first binds
A prokaryotic cluster of genes transcribed as a unit
A protein that blocks RNA polymerase from transcribing a gene
A section of a gene that remains in the mature mRNA
A codon that signals translation to start

questions.q: What is RNA interference?
questions.answer: A natural process that silences specific genes by breaking down their mRNA before it can make proteins
distractors: A natural process that boosts gene expression by making extra copies of mRNA
A mutation that permanently deletes a gene from the DNA
A process that joins exons in different combinations
A process where RNA is copied back into DNA
A repressor protein binding to an operon to block transcription
